title: Terraform safe-guardrails and warm-swap controller for VPC runtime upgrades
creator: Amaya Chen
description: Design and implement a Terraform-driven set of modules and a controller that provide conservative safe-guardrails for zero-downtime warm-swap rollouts of the private (VPC) data-plane runtime. The goal is an IaC-first upgrade path that: (1) expresses phased capacity and canary policies in Terraform, (2) integrates preflight and runtime health checks, (3) performs deterministic state snapshots for rollback, and (4) coordinates cache priming and synthetic probes to avoid user-visible errors during upgrade. This ticket covers module surface design, controller hooks, and the initial implementation for a single-tenant warm-swap flow.
acceptance_criteria:
- Terraform module(s) published in private module registry with versioned releases
- Upgrade pipeline that can run from Terraform apply and perform a staged warm-swap with health gating
- Automated preflight checks (connectivity, KV cache availability, disk/ephemeral sanity) run before traffic cut
- Synthetic probe suite passes for 3 consecutive intervals before shifting >=50% traffic
- Rollback can be triggered from a Terraform apply that restores a captured state snapshot and completes within defined SLO (5 minutes median for single-tenant)
- End-to-end runbook documented and smoke-tested in staging
implementation_notes:
Core components:
1) terraform/modules/warm_swap_umbrella - top-level module that wires capacity, priming, and safety policies
2) terraform/modules/state_snapshot - utility module to capture runtime metadata + KV cache manifest before switchover
3) controller: warm-swap-hooker (k8s operator) invoked by IaC via remote-exec or webhook to coordinate non-idempotent steps (priming, synthetic probe orchestration)
4) healthcheck profiles stored in SSM/Secrets and referenced by Terraform variables
Decision: keep non-destructive and observable operations in Terraform where possible; delegate transient, timing-sensitive coordination (e.g., priming KV cache warmup) to the controller so Terraform remains declarative. Use S3-backed snapshot bundles for deterministic rollback.
updates: 2026-02-26 - Created ticket. Initial scoping and goals documented. Linked to private-runbook template.

2026-03-02 - Spike: implemented prototype terraform module for registering a warm-swap plan (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-iaac/pulls/212). Found that Terraform remote-exec has flakiness for long-lived webhooks; decided to use a webhook + controller pull model.

2026-03-05 - Safety gating: added synthetic-probe checklist and defined traffic shift policy (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) with minimum pass windows. Running priming experiments in staging to calibrate pass thresholds.

2026-03-11 - Integration test passed in staging for a non-primed runtime (cold start) using warm-swap controller; observed 2.3s median extra latency during the 10% shift but no errors. Preparing module documentation for review.
TODO - next: add deterministic snapshot restore path, finalize runbook, and open RFC for ops on emergency rollback triggers.
risks:
- Terraform apply invoking long-running controller hooks can time out; mitigated by switching to webhook + controller pull model.
- Snapshot/restore of KV cache may be large; we will capture manifests and use parallelized priming rather than bulk transfer where possible.
- Incorrect health profile tuning could cause slow rollbacks; include conservative default thresholds and require explicit opt-in for aggressive policies.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for Terraform modules and helper scripts
- Integration test in staging that runs full warm-swap with traffic simulation
- Chaos test: inject a failing synthetic probe during a 30% shift and verify rollback path triggers and completes
- Run manual emergency rollback drill with runbook owners

Security review (Ilya Kovalenko) 2026-03-09: flagged snapshot encryption at rest and access control for S3 manifests; added KMS envelope encryption requirement.
Design feedback (Marta Ruiz) 2026-03-10: recommend separate 'canary priming' step so priming failures do not block small traffic shifts; updated controller plan accordingly.
